To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the competitive effect of ions in sorption of heavy metals onto the solid surfaces depends on the nature of the soil, and the nature of the competing ions.
competitive sorption is strongly affected by the presence of competing ions, which reduce the amount of heavy metal retained by the solid phase and change the sorption isothermal shape.
the sorption of Cd and other metals in soils was affected by competing cations and the presence of Ca in the soil solution was the main cause of this effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the sorption of heavy metals on soils.
the effect of competing ions on the retention capacity of soils and the effect of the competing ions on each other.
the competitive sorption of metals on three soils and the effect of the presence of competing cations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
competitive effects were not the same among metals, but the presence in solution of other ions strongly affected the retention of heavy metals in soil.
the presence of other ions, mainly of Ca, strongly affected metal sorption onto soils.
the presence of competing ions in the soil-solution interface strongly affected heavy metal sorption, but the effect was not uniform for the metals investigated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of Ca, Cu and Pb in soil solution reduces sorption of Ni, Cd and Pb.

in the presence of competing cations the retention of heavy metals is lower, but it can be predicted by the fractional factorial design, and the effect of competing cations is different for each heavy metal.
the presence of competing cations reduces sorption and mobility of the five metals investigated, but the effect depends on the nature of the soil and the cations present.
The main takeaway from our work is that
competition between cations is a key factor that must be taken into consideration in the study and modeling of heavy metal sorption on soil.
the competitive sorption of heavy metals is strongly affected by the presence of competing ions, which can modify the retention capacity of the soil.
the sorption of heavy metals in soils depends on the chemical composition of the system.
